Topic: Why move from research to Data Science & AI?
Content: As a researcher, Alejandro learned that a result only counts if it is reproducible, and he found that Data Science and AI were the best tools to answer complex biological questions at scale. He does not want to leave science behind: he wants to bring that same rigor, plus Machine Learning and generative AI, to Pharma, Health and Life Sciences, where data-driven decisions have a direct impact on patients and research. Having also built and deployed a product end to end (Sextant IA), he can take an analysis or model all the way to production.

Topic: What has been his biggest technical challenge?
Content: During a transcriptomics project, Alejandro faced a severely compromised dataset due to an expired ONT (Nanopore) sequencing flow cell. Instead of discarding the experiment, he engineered a hybrid data rescue strategy using high-fidelity Illumina sequencing data to correct the transcriptome, successfully salvaging the project.

Alejandro's Bachelor's Thesis at CIALE (Universidad de Salamanca) investigated a plant-symbiont-pathogen interaction mechanism. He designed a controlled experiment studying how a genetically modified Trichoderma fungus (symbiont) affected tomato plants' defenses against the Pseudomonas aeruginosa pathogen. By performing qPCR to measure defense hormone gene expression and conducting statistical analysis on leaf infection rates, he successfully demonstrated that the symbiont improved the plant's defense mechanisms.

Alejandro's Master's Thesis at CBMSO (Jan-Sept 2018) focused on biochemical data extraction and enzymatic kinetics. He studied the isolated polymerase domain (polDom) of bacterial Ligase D involved in NHEJ DNA repair. He designed assays to calculate nucleotide insertion kinetics, quantified SDS-PAGE gel images using ImageJ, and performed non-linear statistical curve-fitting (Michaelis-Menten) using GraphPad Prism. By comparing the insertion of DNA versus RNA nucleotides and mismatches, he demonstrated that polDom preferentially inserts RNA bases and tolerates errors. He concluded that during severe stress (NHEJ), the organism prioritizes fast, error-prone DNA repair over leaving lethal double-strand breaks unrepaired.

Alejandro's Master's Thesis focused on the differential analysis of dinoflagellate transcriptomes across different nutrition modes. He engineered an end-to-end bioinformatics pipeline to process massive raw RNA-Seq data. The workflow included quality control (FastQC), trimming (Trimmomatic), contamination filtering (Bowtie2), and de novo transcriptome assembly using Trinity. For downstream analysis, he executed functional annotations (EnTAP, KEGG, GO terms), identified core genes using BUSCO, and built phylogenetic trees. This project perfectly highlights his ability to design robust, automated computational pipelines in Linux/Bash environments to extract insights from massive, unstructured datasets.
